entities.name: sinking of the MV Sewol
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The sinking of the MV Sewol on April 16, 2014, was a devastating maritime disaster that shook South Korea and the world. This ferry tragedy resulted in the loss of 304 lives, mostly students from Danwon High School, who were returning from a school trip. The incident highlighted the country's lax safety regulations and inadequate emergency response. The government's handling of the crisis led to widespread protests and calls for greater accountability. The Sewol disaster had far-reaching consequences, including changes to South Korea's maritime safety laws and a reevaluation of the country's education system. As the country grappled with grief and outrage, the tragedy served as a catalyst for reform and a reminder of the importance of prioritizing human life over economic interests.

The sinking of the MV Sewol was a preventable tragedy that could have been avoided with better safety measures and more rigorous enforcement of regulations. The ferry was carrying over 470 people, including 325 students, when it capsized off the coast of Jindo Island in the Yellow Sea. The incident occurred during a routine voyage from Incheon to Jeju Island, a popular tourist destination. The ferry's route had been altered to avoid paying a toll, which contributed to the overcrowding and subsequent disaster.

The aftermath of the Sewol disaster was marked by outrage and grief, with many calling for greater accountability from the government and the shipping industry. The incident led to changes in South Korea's maritime safety laws and regulations, including stricter enforcement of safety standards and more frequent inspections of ships. The tragedy also prompted a reevaluation of the country's education system, with a focus on improving safety and emergency preparedness.
